description: FamilySearch tree person read for Patrick Flynn WITH relatives and source descriptions — the only init-project fixture that exercises the relationship import, the FAN rule, and the multi-person re-ID to local I/N/F/R/S ids. Wife Mary Kelly, children James and Margaret. ONE parent, father Michael Flynn, and through him ONE sibling, Bridget -- this is the only person_read fixture in which the subject has a parent at all, and therefore the only one that exercises the sibling fan-out this tool performs (it reads each parent to reach siblings, so a subject with zero parents makes zero extra calls and can never produce one). Before 2026-09-21 every one of the seven person-read-* fixtures gave the subject zero parents, so the paid init-project run bought for the fan-out could not observe it. The mother is deliberately still ABSENT and Michael is deliberately unverified: the user's objective is to identify Patrick's parents, and an unproven father attached to a collaborative tree does not answer it -- it is a hypothesis to prove, and Bridget is the FAN lead for proving it. Bridget's 1848 birth is three years off Patrick's ~1845 so the skill's sibling-births-under-nine-months rule has something real to measure and correctly does not fire. Names and relationships arrive without ids, per simplified-gedcomx-spec.md §3 — the caller mints them. Each person does carry an `ark` and each name a `preferred: true`, which person_read always emits: the ark is the only field surviving the re-ID that still points at the FamilySearch person, so dropping it during the copy leaves every tree person unlinked. Facts carry both tool-emitted sidecars (`standard_place`, `standard_date`), neither a string copy of its raw field. One source description carries a `notes` array: person_read emits it, TREE_SOURCE_FIELDS rejects it, so a verbatim copy into the tree fails the project_create write and dropping the whole source to dodge that is the wrong fix. Extended with Patrick's source-style MEMORIES, which this tool returns in the same sources[] array for a non-living subject: memory 228755097 is a family story carrying its full text in `text` (a story's payload text is only a 200-character preview, so the full words come from its artifact), and memory 175960782 is a headstone scan the read's transcription budget did not reach — it still comes back, as metadata whose `notes` says why, and its research.json source takes `transcription: null`. Two further memories on this person are ABSENT ON PURPOSE and their absence is part of what this fixture asserts: the designated portrait, and a family snapshot filed under Photos. Both are dropped by the tool-side filter before the response is built, so a skill must never expect them. Note that the filter is a proxy on media kind — the uploader chooses that kind — so it will also miss a record scan filed under Photos. Both memory sources carry `artifact_url`, the memory ARTIFACT url, which is what `image_transcribe`/`image_read` accept as `memoryArtifactUrl` -- `url` is the human /memories/<id> page and is refused. Like `notes` and `text` it is RESPONSE-ONLY: `TREE_SOURCE_FIELDS` is {id, title, citation, author, url}, so a verbatim copy of one of these rows into tree.gedcomx.json fails the project_create write, and the skill must drop it. Row 175960782 is the budget-skipped memory whose note names that retry route, so without artifact_url the note pointed at a value the row did not contain. The response also carries a top-level `notes` array, which `person_read` emits ONLY when endpoint closure dropped an edge: here Patrick's MOTHER is named in FamilySearch's relationship data without a person record, so her edge cannot be emitted and she is absent from persons[]. This is the only fixture that exercises that key, and it exists because without it nothing checked the half of the 2026-09-21 ruling that matters to a user -- the note reaches the model in the tool result, and the question is whether the skill ever says it out loud. It is a sibling of persons/relationships/sources, never a source field, and must not reach the tree: project_create rebuilds from the three named arrays and discards the rest, so a copy fails nothing loudly -- it just silently is not there. The two strings are verbatim what droppedEdgeNotes emits, so this stays a recording rather than an invention.

sources.title: Patrick Flynn, as remembered by his granddaughter
sources.text: Patrick came over from County Mayo in 1867, a boy of nineteen with his brother Michael. He went into the Schuylkill mines that same winter. He never spoke of the crossing, my mother said, except once, that the water had been very bad. He married Mary Kelly at St. Patrick's in Pottsville and they had the two children, James and Margaret. He was a quiet man and a hard worker, and he died of the miner's asthma in 1908.
